سخني معلقة زيت العود فطنجرة متوسطة.
قلبي نص بصلة مقطعة فالزيت. زيدي 30 غ فرينة وطيبي دقيقة.
زيدي 380 غ فلفلة خضرا مقطعة ديال البواطة، 280 مل مرقة الدجاج، 280 غ صدر الدجاج مطيب ومفتت ونص معلقة تومة مطحونة. خليها تطيب بلا غطاء 5 دقايق.
ذوبي معلقة كبيرة مايزينا ف60 مل ما بارد وزيديها. طيبي 2 دقايق أخرى.
قطعي 8 طورطيات ديال الدرة شرائح وزيديهم على ثلاث مرات. طيبي وحركي حتى يسخنو.
رشي 160 غ فرماج شيدر محكوك من الفوق. غطي وخليها حتى يذوب الفرماج. قدمي دغيا.
tips: إلا ما لقيتيش الفلفلة الخضرا ديال البواطة، قلبي 2 فلفلات خضر مقطعين مع البصلة.
ممكن تحطي كلشي فطبق الفرن وتحمريه 10 دقايق.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (Adapted from Stove Top Casserole Oregon’s Healthy Harvest Recipes Oregon State University Cooperative Extension Service)
name_en: Stove Top Potato and Cabbage Casserole
name_fr: Pommes de terre et chou à la casserole
desc_en: An easy, meatless meal made with potatoes, cabbage, nuts of your choice, and cheese.

ingredients.en: Potatoes, peeled and sliced 1/4 inch thick

steps: Heat oil in large skillet or Dutch oven. Add onions and stir over medium heat until golden.
Add potatoes and chicken stock. Cover tightly, reduce heat to low and simmer until potatoes are almost tender.
Add cabbage, cover and simmer for another 5 minutes.
Remove cover, sprinkle with cheese and nuts.
Let stand just until cheese is melted, about 2 minutes.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (University of Illinois Extension Service)
desc_en: One skillet beef and bean tamale pie that cooks on the stovetop. For an extra kick, add your favorite hot sauce to this tasty tamale pie.

steps: Cook beef in hot skillet until lightly browned. Drain off fat.
Stir in remaining ingredients. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat, cover, and simmer 10 minutes.
tips: Prepare Chili: Prepare Tamale Pie: - Place chili in a 10-inch skillet. Stir in corn. Heat thoroughly. - As chili heats, mix cornmeal and salt with water in a sauce pan. Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly until thickened, about 2 minutes. - Spread cornmeal mixture over hot chili to form a crust. Sprinkle with chili powder. - Cover and cook over low heat, with lid slightly ajar, until topping is set, about 10 minutes. Optional - Top with light sour cream or low-fat yogurt.

steps: طيبي 230 غ كفتة ديال البݣري فمقلة سخانة حتى تحمر. صفي الشحمة.

زيدي 55 غ لوبيا حمرا مع 55 مل من الما ديالها، 150 غ ماطيشة مهرسة، معلقة كبيرة بصلة مقطعة، ربع معلقة كبيرة شيلي مطحون، 420 غ درة، 70 غ سميدة ديال الدرة، رشة ملحة، 300 مل ما بارد وربع معلقة صغيرة شيلي. حركي وخليها تغلي.
نقصي النار، غطي وخليها 10 دقايق حتى تخثر السميدة.
tips: حركي من وقت لوقت باش ما تلصقش السميدة.
رشي فرماج محكوك فالأخير إلا بغيتي.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (Produce for Better Health Foundation)
name_en: Strawberries, White Bean, and Edamame Salad
name_fr: Salade fraises, haricots blancs et edamame
name_latin: Chladat fraise o loubya bida o edamame
desc_en: A flavorful, enticing mix of fresh strawberries, white beans, and edamame in a light vinaigrette nested on a baby spinach and topped with crumbled feta cheese.

steps: Cook edamame according to package directions, while preparing remaining ingredients.
Rinse under cool water and drain.
In a small bowl, whisk vinaigrette ingredients.
In a medium bowl, toss all ingredients except spinach and vinaigrette.
Serve on individual plates by nesting strawberry, white bean and edamame mix atop spinach.
Drizzle with dressing.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (MyPlate National Strategic Partners The Grain Chain)
desc_en: Enjoy the flavors of layered strawberries, crispy cereal flakes, and creamy yogurt in this delicious parfait. Serve as a fruit-filled breakfast option or a better-for-you dessert!

ingredients.en: Bran and wheat flakes ready-to-eat cereal

steps: Stir banana and vanilla into yogurt and combine well.
In a 10 to 12 ounce glass, alternately layer the yogurt-banana mixture, strawberries, and cereal.
Serve immediately and enjoy.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion)
name_latin: Glace danone bel fraise o kiwi
desc_en: Cool off with frozen pops that are fun to make! Mix different yogurt and fruit combinations to find your favorite.

steps: Cut fruit into small pieces.
Mix fruit and yogurt.
Divide into 4 small paper cups (or 8 ice cubes) and place in popsicle sticks (or cut paper straws).
Freeze.
Enjoy as a frozen treat!

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (Produce for Better Health Foundation)
name_latin: Khobz mhammer bel fraise o manga o feta
desc_en: Diced strawberries, mango, and fat-free feta cheese provide the perfect balance of sweet, savory, and tangy for these quick and colorful brunch or lunch toast points.

steps: Peel and pit mango. Dice 3/4 of mango and 3/4 of strawberries; place in large bowl with feta cheese. Put remaining fruit, 1/4 cup basil, vinegar, and oil in a blender and blend.
Pour blended vinaigrette over fruit-feta mix and toss gently.
Chop remaining basil leaves.
Toast bread slices and cut each slice diagonally.
Top toast points with dressed fruit-feta mix and chopped basil.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (University of Maryland Cooperative Extension Food Supplement Nutrition Education Program The University of Connecticut, SNAP4CT (photo))
desc_en: No campfire required for these fruity graham cracker snacks!

steps: Rinse the strawberries in water.
Slice the strawberries.
Add the yogurt and strawberries to 1/2 of graham cracker.
Top with the other 1/2 of graham cracker.
Enjoy immediately.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion)
name_fr: Glaces au yaourt à la fraise
desc_en: Strawberries and yogurt are all you need for this healthy frozen snack! They're a great after school snack or late night dessert!

steps: Cut strawberries into small pieces.
Mix fruit and yogurt.
Divide into 4 small paper cups (or 8 ice cubes) and place in popsicle sticks (or cut paper straws).
Freeze.
Enjoy as a frozen treat!

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (Adapted from "Wonderful Stuffed Potatoes" A Healthier You: Based on the Dietary Guidelines for Americans US Department of Health and Human Services Office of Disease Prevention and Health Promotion)
name_fr: Pommes de terre farcies au four
desc_en: Pair these delicious stuffed potatoes with grilled or baked meat, fish, or tofu.

steps: Prick potatoes with fork. Bake at 425 degrees F for 60 minutes or until fork is easily inserted.
Cut potatoes in half lengthwise. Carefully scoop out potato, leaving about 1/2 inch of pulp inside shell. Mash pulp in large bowl.
Mix remaining ingredients with the mashed potato, except Parmesan cheese. Spoon mixture into potato shells.
Sprinkle top of each stuffed potato with Parmesan cheese.
Place on baking sheet and return to oven. Bake 15 to 20 minutes or until tops are golden brown.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (Simple Healthy Recipes Oklahoma Nutrition Information and Education ONIE Project)
desc_en: Peppers stuffed with a combination of ground beef, brown rice, veggies, and spices create a filling dish. Try using red, green, yellow, and orange bell peppers for a colorful meal. Enjoy with a side of low-fat cottage cheese and canned pineapple.

steps: Cut a circular hole in the tops of the bell peppers. Remove seeds and membrane and set aside.
In a large bowl, combine remaining ingredients and stir until completely mixed. Fill the bell peppers with meat mixture.
Place the stuffed bell peppers in large stock pot on stove, with the tops facing up. Add 1-inch water to bottom of pot and cover.
Place heat on medium, keeping covered for 30 to 40 minutes until rice is done. Serve.
قطعي دائرة فراس 5 فلفلات وحيدي الزريعة من الداخل.
فطبسيل كبير خلطي 450 غ كفتة ديال البݣري، 140 غ روز كامل، 200 غ ماطيشة مقطعة ديال البواطة، 3 معالق عصير الحامض، ربع معلقة قرفة، ربع معلقة نافع وربع معلقة إبزار. عمري الفلفلة بالخليط.
حطي الفلفلة المعمرة واقفة فطنجرة كبيرة. زيدي 3 سم ما فالقاع وغطي.
خليها تطيب على نار متوسطة مغطية 30 حتى 40 دقيقة حتى يطيب الروز.
tips: القرفة والنافع كيعطيو طعم شرقي زوين للكفتة.
إلا الما سالا قبل ما يطيب الروز، زيدي شوية.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (From Pyramid to the Plate: Healthy Eating by Timing, Combining, and Planning Adopted from: Eating Right is Basic Michigan State University Extension)
desc_en: These tasty stuffed peppers make a delicious and filling entrée. Use brown rice to increase your whole grains.

steps: Cut around the stem of the green bell peppers. Remove the seeds and the pulpy part of the peppers.
Wash, and then cook peppers in boiling water for five minutes. Drain well.
In saucepan, brown turkey. Add rice, onion, 1/2 cup tomato sauce, and black pepper.
Stuff each pepper with the mixture and place in casserole dish.
Pour the remaining tomato sauce over the green peppers.
Cover and bake for 30 minutes at 350 °F.
قطعي راس 4 فلفلات خضر كبار وحيدي الزريعة من الداخل.
غسليهم وطيبيهم فما مغلي 5 دقايق. صفيهم مزيان.
فطنجرة حمري 450 غ كفتة الديك الرومي. زيدي 180 غ روز، 75 غ بصلة مقطعة، 120 مل من صلصة الماطيشة ورشة إبزار.
عمري كل فلفلة بالخليط وحطيهم فطبق الفرن.
صبي باقي 380 مل صلصة الماطيشة فوق الفلفلة.
غطي ودخلي للفرن على 180 درجة 30 حتى 40 دقيقة حتى يطيب الروز.
tips: إلا استعملتي روز نيء، زيدي 10 دقايق وشوية ما فالصلصة.
ممكن تستعملي كفتة البݣري بلاصة الديك الرومي.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (Spend Smart. Eat Smart, Adapted from Easy Stuffed Pasta Shells Iowa State University Extension)
desc_en: Spinach, a mixture of low-fat cheeses, and herbs combine for a delicious filling in these stuffed shells.

ingredients.en: Light tomato basil pasta sauce, low-sodium

steps: Preheat oven to 375 °F. Lightly coat a 13x9x2 inch baking dish with cooking spray. Set aside.

Drain spinach by placing in a sieve or colander over the sink, or in a bowl and pressing with a spool to remove as much liquid as possible, or squeeze out liquid with clean hands. Place spinach in medium bowl.
Add the cottage cheese, 1 cup of the mozzarella cheese, oregano, and pepper to the spinach. Stir to mix thoroughly.
Pour half of the spaghetti sauce into prepared baking dish. Add water and stir into the mix.
Spoon about 3 tablespoons cheese mixture into each uncooked pasta shell and arrange in a single layer over top.
Sprinkle with remaining 1/2 cup mozzarella cheese evenly over sauce.
Cover tightly with foil. Bake for 1 hour or until shells are tender. Let stand 10 minutes before serving.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (Connecticut Food Policy Council)
desc_en: Summer squash stuffed with brown rice, fresh basil, beans, cheese, and veggies make a hearty and filling dish. Try this tasty recipe when summer squash are abundant in your garden or at the market.

steps: Wash and cut squash in half, lengthwise. Remove the large seeds.
Steam the squash, skin side down, in a small amount of water in a fry pan or skillet until slightly tender (but not mushy).
Scoop out a good amount of pulp (1 cup), place in a bowl and mix with stuffing (brown rice through Parmesan cheese).
Place the squash shells in a baking dish. Stuff the squash with the stuffing mixture.
Top with grated Parmesan cheese. Bake at 350 °F for about 30 minutes.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (Pennsylvania Nutrition Education Network)
desc_en: Stuffed tomatoes make a delicious side dish to the Baked Chicken with Vegetables, both dishes bake at 400 °F, add the stuffed tomatoes to the oven for the last 20 minutes of bake time.

steps: Preheat the oven to 400 °F.
Peel the onion. Chop it into small pieces.
Cut each tomato in half. Remove the part with the stem.
Gently squeeze each tomato half over the sink to remove the seeds.
Put the breadcrumbs into medium bowl. Add the spices and oil.
Mix well, slowly adding water to moisten the crumbs.
Use a spoon to press the crumb mixture into the tomato halves.
Lightly oil a baking pan. Place the tomatoes on the pan, with the cut side up.
Bake for 15 to 20 minutes, until the crumbs are browned and the tomatoes are soft.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (Washington State University Extension)
name_en: Sugar and Spice Cookies (from Better Baking Mix)
desc_en: Use our Better Baking Mix for this quick and easy recipe. You can double the recipe if baking for a crowd.

steps: Preheat oven to 350 °F. Lightly grease baking sheet.
In a mixing bowl, combine baking mix, sugar, cinnamon, and raisins (optional). Stir to mix.
Put oil, egg, and vanilla in a small bowl. Beat with a fork to mix.
Add oil and egg mix to the dry ingredients.
Stir to combine. Dough will be thick.
Measure level tablespoons of dough. Drop on cookie sheet about 2 inches apart. Dough with spread into cookies 2 1/2 to 3 inches wide as it bakes.
Bake 10 to 12 minutes or until edges start to turn brown. Be careful not to overbake.
Remove cookies from baking sheet while still warm.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (Heart Healthy Home Cooking: African American Style US Department of Health and Human Services National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute)
desc_en: A delicious smoothie makes the perfect summer snack or dessert.

steps: Place all ingredients in blender and purée until smooth.
Serve in frosted glass.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (University of Nebraska-Lincoln Cooperative Extension)
desc_en: Toss this fruit salad together in a flash. Doubles and triples easily for a large group.

ingredients.en: Pineapple chunks, fresh or canned packed in natural juice

steps: Stir fruit together in a medium-sized bowl.
Cover and chill. Serve as soon as possible.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (Eating Smart, Being Active Colorado State University and University of California at Davis)
desc_en: Fresh tomatoes, summer squash, green peppers, and onions give this cheesy side dish a boost to any summer meal. Use any vegetables that you have on hand or find at the Farmers Market.

steps: Preheat oven to 350 °F.
Combine onion, squash, tomato, and green pepper in a baking dish.
Sprinkle with oregano.
Pour the tomato sauce over the vegetables.
Bake, uncovered at 350 °F for 20 to 30 minutes.
Top with cheese and bake another 4 to 5 minutes until cheese is melted.
Refrigerate leftovers.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (Creative Vegetable Cookery North Dakota State University Extension Service)
desc_en: This salad can be tossed together, lightening fast. Walnuts give this salad a delightful crunch. Enjoy as a tasty side dish.

steps: Wash and dry greens. Tear into bite-sized pieces and place in large salad bowl.
Add onion, mushrooms, walnuts, and parsley. Just before serving, toss with dressing.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (Farm Fresh Summertime Recipes Connecticut Food Policy Council)
desc_en: Fresh sweet basil and cheese give summer squash a burst of flavor.

steps: Using a large, oven-proof frying pan, heat 1 tablespoon of oil on medium-high.
Arrange squash in pan, add water, and season lightly with salt, pepper, and basil.
Cover and cook over medium heat for 5 minutes, or until tender crisp.
Sprinkle with cheese and drizzle with remaining oil. Place under a preheated broiler and broil until cheese melts and browns slightly.
tips: Tip: Add cut up fresh tomatoes, green peppers, green beans, eggplant, onions, or other vegetables in season.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (University of Maryland Cooperative Extension Food Supplement Nutrition Education Program)
desc_en: Garlic powder and onion give summer veggies a nice flavor. Combined with canned tomatoes, this dish can be eaten as a side dish or serve over whole grain pasta or brown rice.

ingredients.en: Yellow summer squash, small and sliced

steps: In large skillet, heat oil.
To heated oil, add squash and onion. Cook on medium heat until tender, about 10 minutes, stirring often.
Add tomatoes and simmer 5 minutes.
Season with garlic powder to taste. Add salt and pepper (optional), if desired.
Serve warm, topped with Parmesan cheese.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (Adapted from Squash Squares, Farm Fresh Summertime Recipes Connecticut Food Policy Council)
desc_en: This side dish is great for a big holiday meal or potluck. Try it with different veggies for a fun twist.

steps: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F.
Mix all ingredients thoroughly and pour into a greased 13x9-inch baking dish.
Bake in preheated oven for 25 minutes, or until bubbly and brown.
Cut into 8 squares and serve while warm.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (Connecticut Food Policy Council)
desc_en: Jazz up this summer dish by adding cumin, garlic powder, or fresh basil.

steps: In a skillet (the larger the better), heat oil on medium-high heat.
Add onion and stir fry until onion is clear and begins to brown.
Add carrots and stir until carrots are tender and crisp. Add squash and cook for about 2 minutes. Lower heat.
Add seasonings of choice. Cook for 2 more minutes. Serve as a side dish.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (Stay Young at Heart: Cooking the Heart-Healthy Way US Department of Health and Human Services National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute)
desc_en: This tasty pasta dish is packed full of delicious veggies. Enjoy with fruit on the side.

steps: Combine first 10 ingredients in large saucepan. Cook for 10 minutes (up to black pepper), then stir in tomato paste. Cover and cook gently, 15 minutes, stirring occasionally until vegetables are tender.
Cook spaghetti in unsalted water according to package directions.
Spoon sauce over drained hot spaghetti and sprinkle Parmesan cheese over top.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (Stay Young at Heart: Cooking the Heart-Healthy Way US Department of Health and Human Services National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute)
desc_en: Hot sauce and almonds make this rice dish explode with flavor. Only one pot is needed making this an easy and delicious side dish.

steps: Heat oil in medium saucepan. Add celery and onions and saute until tender, about 10 minutes.
Add water, juices, and hot sauce. Bring to a boil. Stir in rice and bring back to a boil. Let stand covered until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed.
Stir in almonds. Serve immediately as a side dish for a fish entree.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (US Department of Health and Human Services)
desc_en: Oranges help to brighten up this tasty veggie salad. It is quick and easy to make. Top it off with your favorite vinaigrette.

steps: Toss all ingredients together in a large bowl. Add dressing and toss again.
Serve immediately.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (Healthy Snacks University of Wisconsin Cooperative Extension Service)
name_en: Sure to Please Baked Eggs & Cheese
desc_en: Add your favorite veggies to dress up this cheese and egg dish, or serve with fresh salsa.

steps: Preheat oven to 350 °F.
Put oil in a medium baking dish or small cake pan and heat in the oven for a few minutes.
In a bowl, beat eggs. Mix in remaining ingredients. Pour into hot pan.
Bake 20 minutes or until eggs are firm. Serve immediately.
tips: * 4 eggs and 4 egg whites may be used instead of 6 eggs to reduce fat and cholesterol (nutrient analysis reflects this modification).

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen
desc_en: This fish taco recipe is a time and money saver, using canned tuna and a mix of canned and fresh veggies.

ingredients.en: Lime juice or juice from one lime
Grain tortillas or hard taco shells

steps: In a medium bowl, flake tuna with fork. Stir in beans, corn, mayonnaise, taco seasoning*, and lime juice.
Place lettuce, cheese, and salsa in separate bowls.
Place tortillas or taco shells on microwave safe plate. Microwave on high for 1 minute.**
To eat, layer tuna mixture, lettuce, and cheese on tortilla. Top with salsa.
فطبسيل فتتي 400 غ طون بالفرشيطة. زيدي 400 غ لوبيا حمرا مصفية، 150 غ درة، 80 غ مايونيز خفيف، 2 معالق توابل الطاكو و2 معالق عصير الليم. حركي.
حطي 120 غ خس محكوك، 160 غ فرماج شيدر محكوك و120 غ صالصا فطبسيلات منفصلين.
سخني 12 طورطيا فالميكرو دقيقة ولا فمقلة ناشفة.
كل واحد يعمر الطورطيا ديالو: الطون، الخس، الفرماج والصالصا من الفوق.
tips: توابل الطاكو: كامون، شيلي مطحون، تومة مطحونة، أوريݣانو.
طبق بارد سريع بلا طياب، مزيان للصيف.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (Pennsylvania Nutrition Education Network)
desc_en: Squash baked in the oven and then seasoned with cinnamon and nutmeg give this dish a taste of fall.

steps: Put each squash in the microwave. Heat for 1 1/2 minutes on high. This will soften the squash, and make it easier to cut.
Cut each squash in half. Remove the seeds and loosen fibers in the middle.
Place the squash on an ungreased baking pan. The cut side of the squash should be face-up, and the uncut part of the squash should touch the pan.
Pour 2 tablespoons of juice into each half of the squash. Spread it evenly on the inside of each squash.
Bake at 400 °F for 30 to 45 minutes, until tender.
Season with cinnamon and nutmeg, and serve.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (Produce for Better Health Foundation)
desc_en: Traditional tapenades can be high in sodium, but not this version, with its base of raisins. Spread on crackers or pita bread as a snack or appetizer, or include as part of a tapas-inspired meal. Makes a great portable lunch.

steps: Place tapenade ingredients in food processor.
Run until raisins, olives, and walnuts are finely chopped.
Can be made ahead and refrigerated.
Serve with melba rounds or pita wedges.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (Pennsylvania Nutrition Education Network)
desc_en: This tangy cabbage dish requires no cooking. Chill for several hours and serve as a side dish for lunch or dinner.

steps: Cut the cabbage in half and rinse it with water.
Chop the cabbage into very thin bit-sized slices.
In a large bowl, combine ingredients and mix well.
Cover the bowl.
Chill in the fridge for several hours before serving.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (Favorite Recipes for Family Meals Washington State University Extension)
desc_en: Only three ingredients in this fast and easy dressing. Served chilled over your favorite salad.

steps: In a small saucepan, combine sugar and cornstarch.
Stir in vinegar.
Cook over medium heat until slightly thickened and clear.
Chill before serving. Store refrigerated.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (Cooking Healthy with Diabetes University of Florida IFAS Extension)
desc_en: Lemon juice, honey, soy sauce, and pineapple juice make the base of this delicious sweet and sour sauce. Enjoy!

steps: Combine all ingredients except vegetables into bowl; mix and set aside.
Heat 2 teaspoons of oil in skillet and add frozen vegetables. Cook for 3 to 4 minutes or until vegetables are crisp-tender.
Add sweet and sour sauce and cook for another 2 minutes or until mixture comes to a boil. Add water if it seems too thick.
Serve immediately. This dish is great over pasta or brown rice.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (Honor the Gift of Food: Learn at Home Lessons Indian Health Service Division of Diabetes Treatment and Prevention)
name_en: Sweet Cornmeal Pudding with Ginger and Cinnamon
name_fr: Pudding de maïs sucré au gingembre et cannelle
name_latin: Pudding dra bel skenjbir o qerfa
desc_en: This baked pudding combines milk and cornmeal with spices to produce a custard-like dessert that you can serve on special occasions.

steps: Preheat oven to 325 °F. Lightly grease 1-quart baking pan.
In a saucepan, heat 2 1/2 cups of milk to a simmer.
In a bowl, mix together the other 1/2 cup cold milk with cornmeal.
Add cornmeal mixture to warm milk, stir well.
Cook 20 minutes over low-medium heat. Stir often to prevent scorching. Cook until thickened.
Remove pudding from heat. Stir in margarine, molasses, ginger and cinnamon.
Pour into the greased baking pan.
Bake for 55 to 60 minutes. When a knife is inserted and comes out clean, the pudding is done.
Cut into 8 squares before serving. Serve warm.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (Eating Smart, Being Active Colorado State University and University of California at Davis)
name_latin: Btata hlowa o tfah fel ferran
desc_en: Enjoy the taste of fall with the combination of sweet potatoes and apples in this delicious side dish. Serve with roasted chicken or turkey, and a large green salad.

steps: Preheat oven to 350 °F.
Put sweet potatoes in baking dish.
Add apples.
Pour 2 tablespoons of the sweet potato liquid over the mixture.
Mix brown sugar, nuts, flour, and melted butter together in a small bowl.
Sprinkle over the top of the sweet potato/apple mix.
Bake for 20 to 30 minutes, until the top is golden brown and bubbly.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (A Harvest of Recipes with USDA Foods USDA Food Distribution Program on Indian Reservations)
desc_en: Sweet potato casserole is rich is flavor and low in fat.

ingredients.en: Low-sodium sweet potatoes, drained and chopped

steps: Preheat oven to 350 °F.
In a small bowl, combine milk, brown sugar, cinnamon, and oatmeal. Mix well and set aside.
In a medium-sized baking pan, add the sweet potatoes so that they cover the bottom of the pan.
Add the oatmeal mixture on top of the sweet potatoes.
Bake for 20 minutes. Serve hot or refrigerate and serve cold.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (Food and Health Communications, Inc.)
desc_en: Cinnamon, nutmeg, and ginger combined with vanilla extract are a delicious backdrop for sweet potatoes. Use canned sweet potatoes if you don't have whole sweet potatoes on hand. This recipe would be great for Thanksgiving.

steps: Rinse sweet potatoes in cold running water and pierce with a fork.
Microwave sweet potatoes on full power until tender, about 15 minutes. Turn them half way during baking.
Preheat oven to 400 degrees. Remove skin from sweet potatoes and mash with hand beaters or food processor. Add the rest of the ingredients and mix until smooth.
Pour mixture in an 8 inch baking dish. Bake until casserole is firm in the center, about 40 minutes.
Remove pan from oven. Allow to stand for 5 minutes then cut into 10 squares.
Serve hot. Refrigerate leftovers.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (Eat Smart New York! Cornell University Cooperative Extension)
desc_en: Make this delicious and creamy cheesecake full of fall spice flavor for your next holiday celebration.

ingredients.fr: Mélange d'épices pour tarte (cannelle, gingembre, muscade)

steps: Combine crumbs and butter.
Press mixture into bottom and 1 inch up sides of an 8 inch spring form pan. Set aside.
tips: Wash hands with soap and water. Crust: Filling: - In a large mixing bowl, beat cream cheese, sweet potatoes, egg white, sugar, pumpkin pie spice, orange peel, and the vanilla until combined. DO NOT OVER BEAT. - Stir in milk. Carefully pour into prepared pan. - Bake at 350 °F for 60 to 70 minutes until center appears set. - Cool on wire rack for 45 minutes. Cover and chill thoroughly. - Remove sides of pan. - Garnish with dessert topping and orange peel.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (US Department of Health and Human Services)
desc_en: This custard is sweet and creamy and is a wonderful dessert or a sweet treat as a snack.

steps: In a medium bowl, stir together sweet potato and banana.
Add milk, blending well.
Add brown sugar, egg yolks, and salt, mixing thoroughly.
Spray casserole dish with non-stick cooking spray. Transfer sweet potato mixture to casserole dish.
Bake in preheated 325 °F oven for 35 minutes. Remove from oven.
Combine raisins, sugar, and cinnamon; sprinkle over top of sweet potato mixture.
Return to oven and bake 10 more minutes.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (Created by Brighter Bites, a member of the MyPlate National Strategic Partnership Program)
desc_en: This salad has all of the warmth, sweetness, and crunch in a salad to keep you wanting more! This dish goes well in a lunchbox with a sandwich or pairs perfectly with a grilled chicken breast. This salad is kid-tested and mom-approved!

steps: Preheat oven to 400 °F.
Drizzle diced sweet potatoes with 1 teaspoon of olive oil and roast in the oven on a baking sheet for 10 minutes.
Once sweet potatoes are cooked, remove from the oven and allow them to cool.
In a large mixing bowl, combine the sweet potato, apples, pomegranate seeds, and pepitas.
Whisk the remaining 1/2 tablespoon of olive oil, apple cider vinegar, salt, and pepper in a separate bowl.
Once mixed, add to sweet potato mixture and toss until the salad is lightly coated.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion)
name_fr: Hachis de patate douce à l'œuf
desc_en: The unique hash is made with sweet potatoes sautéed with chicken beef sausage, onion, bell pepper, and garlic. Top with a pan-fried egg for a delicious breakfast.

ingredients.fr: Saucisses de poulet ou de bœuf

steps: Put sweet potatoes and water in a skillet and bring to a boil over high heat.
Reduce heat to low and cook about 20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the water has been absorbed by the sweet potatoes.

Add oil, beef sausage, onion, bell pepper and garlic to the skillet with the sweet potatoes. Cook about 20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the onion is lightly browned and the sweet potatoes are tender.
Divide the hash between 4 plates and return the skillet to the stove.
Reheat the skillet over medium high heat and when it is hot, add the remaining 1 teaspoon oil.
Add the eggs, one at a time, and cook about 3 to 5 minutes until the whites are solid and the yolks begin to thicken but are not hard. Flip the egg and cook for one more minute.
Top sweet potato hash with an egg and serve right away.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (Produce for Better Health Foundation)
name_en: Sweet Potato Pancakes with Balsamic Maple Mushrooms
name_fr: Pancakes de patate douce aux champignons balsamiques
desc_en: This healthful version of pancakes features the delicious goodness of mashed sweet potatoes and whole grains, artfully balanced with sweet savory sautéed mushrooms infused with maple syrup and balsamic vinegar. This dish is perfect for dinner or brunch.

ingredients.en: Cremini and/or white button mushrooms, quartered

steps: Microwave sweet potatoes until soft; let cool. Peel and mash potatoes, using an electric mixer.
Add milk, egg, and vegetable oil to potatoes; mix. Sift together dry ingredients and add to potato mixture. Mix on low until just blended.
Heat non-stick skillet or griddle over medium heat; coat skillet with cooking spray.
Use 1/4 cup of batter per pancake, ladling into hot skillet. Wait until pancake bubbles and looks slightly dry on top before flipping over.
While pancakes are cooking, heat 1 tablespoon vegetable oil in another skillet (do not use non-stick) over medium flame.
Add quartered mushrooms and toss coat with oil. Let simmer, stirring occasionally, until juices run.
Add maple syrup and balsamic vinegar to pan. Let simmer until sauce reduces and thickens.
To serve, stack 2 or 3 pancakes, alternating with balsamic maple mushrooms.
طيبي 3 حبات بطاطا حلوة فالميكرو حتى يطراو، خليهم يبردو، قشريهم وهرسيهم.
زيدي 240 مل حليب، بيضة مخفوقة و2 معالق زيت وخلطي. غربلي 120 غ فرينة كاملة، 2 معالق صغار خميرة الحلوة وربع معلقة ملحة وزيديهم. خلطي بشوية.
سخني مقلة على نار متوسطة ودهنيها بشوية زيت.
صبي ربع كاس من العجين لكل بانكيك. قلبيه ملي يبان فيه الفقاقيع ويولي ناشف من الفوق.
فمقلة أخرى سخني معلقة زيت على نار متوسطة.
زيدي 450 غ فقاع مقطع على ربعة وقلبيه بالزيت. خليه يطيب وحركي حتى يخرج الما ديالو.
زيدي 110 غ عسل (ولا سيرو المابل) ومعلقة خل بالزاميك. خليها تخثر.
قدمي 2 ولا 3 بانكيكات مع الفقاع بينهم.
tips: طبق حلو ومالح غريب شوية لكن بنين، جربيه.
البانكيك ديال البطاطا الحلوة كيمشي أيضا مع العسل وحده للفطور.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (USDA Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP))
desc_en: Jazz up traditional pancakes by adding spices and sweet potatoes. Increase your fruits by topping with homemade applesauce.

ingredients.fr: Mélange d'épices pour tarte (cannelle, gingembre, muscade)

ingredients.en: Mashed sweet potatoes -- or winter squash or pumpkin
ingredients.fr: Purée de patate douce ou de courge

steps: Combine all ingredients and stir just until large lumps disappear. Note: Over-stirring will result in tough pancakes.
Pour slightly less than 1/4 cup batter for each pancake onto skillet or electric griddle heated to 350 to 375 °F.
When pancakes bubble around edges and towards center, sprinkle with chopped nuts (if you choose). Then, flip pancakes.
Pancake is done when bottoms are golden brown.
Serve with applesauce or syrup.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (Pennsylvania Nutrition Education Network)
desc_en: Mashed sweet potatoes are coated in bread crumbs and lightly fried in a pan for an easy side dish. Enjoy with a fresh green salad, and whole grain toast, or brown rice.

steps: Wash the sweet potatoes.
Bake the sweet potatoes in a microwave until they are soft.
Remove the peels from the sweet potatoes.
Put the sweet potatoes in a medium bowl. Mash them with a fork.
Crush the bread crumbs on a cutting board with a rolling pin or jar.
Put the crushed bread crumbs in a small bowl.
Shape sweet potato into 6 small patties.
Roll each patty in the crushed crumbs.
Heat the oil in a frying pan on medium heat.
Brown each patty on both sides in the oil.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (Opening the Door to Good Health Cookbook: Healthy Recipes from Around the World Ohio Commission on Minority Health)
desc_en: A delicious holiday favorite! You can use canned sweet potato if you don't have time to roast and mash your own!

steps: Beat egg whites well.
Add sugar, orange juice, orange rind, spices, margarine, and salt.
Add mashed sweet potatoes and mix thoroughly.
Pour into pie shell and bake in preheated 350 °F oven for 1 hour or until firm.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (North Dakota Food and Culture: A Taste of World Cuisine North Dakota State University Extension Service)
desc_en: Ground ginger and molasses are combined with mashed sweet potatoes and cooked in the oven for a delicious dessert.

steps: In a 3 quart saucepan, combine sweet potatoes, molasses, ginger, baking powder, salt, and vegetable oil.
Simmer slowly, stirring constantly, for 10 minutes.
Pour into well-greased 9 inch baking pan.
Bake at 325 °F for 30 minutes, stirring every five minutes for the first 20 minutes.
Smooth down the top and allow to brown.
Cut into squares and serve hot or cold.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (University of Arkansas Division of Agriculture)
name_en: Sweet and Savory Peanut Butter Dip
name_fr: Dip au beurre de cacahuète sucré-salé
name_latin: M3joun zebdat kawkaw hlou o maleh
desc_en: This creamy dip is a great after-school snack! In addition to celery, you can serve it with apples, carrots, jicama, or bell peppers.

steps: Combine peanut butter, apple butter, milk, and soy sauce in a small bowl.
Whisk together until very smooth.
Store tightly, sealed in refrigerator.
Serve with celery or other crunchy fruits and vegetables.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (Pennsylvania Nutrition Education Network)
desc_en: Vegetable oil is used to make this sweet and sour salad dressing.

steps: Mix all ingredients and stir or shake well.
Chill in the fridge for at least 1 hour before serving. Store in the fridge in a bottle or container.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (Favorite Recipes for Family Meals Washington State University Extension)
desc_en: Make your own sweetened condensed milk for your holiday dessert needs.

steps: In order listed, put ingredients into a blender and blend until smooth.
Store in the refrigerator for up to one week.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (Virginia Cooperative Extension - www.eatsmartmovemoreva.org)

steps: In a skillet, heat oil over medium heat. Add onions and cook until softened.
Add the Swiss chard stems and continue to sauté until beginning to soften.
Increase the heat to high and add the Swiss chard leaves and dried cranberries.
Once the chard is wilted, turn off the heat and cover the skillet, letting it rest for a few minutes before serving.
For softer greens, let them rest a little longer.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (California Health Department, Los Angeles County Es Facil Campaign)
desc_en: Potatoes are coated with taco seasoning and corn meal then baked in the oven until golden brown.

steps: Preheat oven to 400 °F.
Wash and scrub potatoes well. Cut the potatoes in half, lengthwise and then into wedges.
Place potatoes in large mixing bowl, toss with the olive oil until potatoes are well coated.
Sprinkle the seasonings and corn meal over potatoes, toss again until coated.
Arrange the potatoes on a baking sheet.
Bake for approximately 30 minutes until potatoes are golden brown.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (Favorite Recipes for Family Meals Washington State University Extension)
desc_en: Ground beef and beans are flavored with cumin and chili powder and served over lettuce and other veggies for an easy weeknight dinner. Top with cheese and dressing.

steps: Brown ground beef and drain any fat.
Add beans, cumin, and chili powder and heat through.
Toss lettuce, tomatoes, onion, and cheese in large bowl.
Spoon on meat and bean mixture and top with broken tortilla chips.
Prepare dressing by mixing yogurt and salsa. Serve on the side of the salad
Refrigerate leftovers within two hours.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (Simply Good Eating Recipe Cards, Vol. 1, 2000 University of Minnesota Cooperative Extension Service)
desc_en: Add some low-sodium taco seasoning to spice up this ground beef and bean taco salad.

ingredients.ar: كفتة ديال الديك الرومي ولا البݣري

steps: Put lettuce in large bowl. Add tomatoes and green pepper.
Brown meat and onion in fry pan. Drain off fat and liquid.
Mix meat, beans, and salsa. Add to salad mixture.
Serve with additional salsa. Refrigerate leftovers.
حطي 180 غ خس مقطع فطبسيل كبير. زيدي 2 ماطيشات و75 غ فلفلة خضرا مقطعين.
حمري 450 غ كفتة (ديك رومي ولا بݣري) مع بصلة مقطعة فمقلة. صفي الشحمة والما.
خلطي الكفتة مع 55 غ لوبيا و190 غ صالصا. زيديهم للشلاضة.
قدمي مع صالصا زيادة.
tips: زيدي شوية كامون وشيلي للكفتة وهي كتطيب.
رشي شيبس الطورطيا مهرس من الفوق للقرمشة.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (2009 Recipe Calendar University of Maryland Extension Food Supplement Nutrition Education Program)
desc_en: Top this ground beef and bean taco soup with shredded lettuce and fat-free sour cream or nonfat yogurt for the full taco experience.

steps: Brown meat in a pot over medium heat.
Put meat in a strainer to drain fat. Rinse with hot water.
Mix all the ingredients in the same pot and cook on low for an hour.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (Fix it Fresh! Recipe Series Kansas State University Research and Extension)
name_en: Tangy Crisp Vegetable and Pasta Salad
name_fr: Salade croquante de pâtes et légumes
desc_en: Use your favorite pasta and veggies to make this salad a family favorite. Make a day ahead and allow to chill in the refrigerator overnight so the flavors blend.

steps: Cook pasta according to package directions, but do not add salt to cooking water.
Drain, rinse with cool water, and drain again.
In a small saucepan, combine vinegar, sugar, garlic powder, and black pepper.
Stir over medium heat until sugar is dissolved, but do not boil. Let cool.
Rinse, drain, and chop remaining ingredients. Combine in a shallow container.
Add cooked pasta and vinegar mixture. Mix gently.
Cover and refrigerate overnight to allow flavors to blend.
Top with parsley and serve cold.
Cover and refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (Iowa Department of Public Health Iowa Nutrition Network)
desc_en: Jicama provides a wonderful crunchy texture for this tasty and tangy slaw.

steps: Cut the jicama in half so you have a flat side for stability.
Peel the jicama using a small sharp knife.
Cut the jicama in small strips or grate it using a large hand grater.
Stir all the ingredients together in a bowl and enjoy.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (Creative Vegetable Cookery North Dakota State University Extension Service)
desc_en: This tasty, tangy dressing compliments salads that feature citrus fruit. Nutmeg adds an extra kick.

steps: Mix milk, concentrate, and nutmeg.
Shake well before using.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (Food Hero Oregon State University Cooperative Extension Service)
desc_en: A cost-effective alternative to store-bought tartar sauce. Use this sauce with your favorite seafood at home and it will not disappoint.

steps: In a small bowl, combine all the ingredients.
Serve immediately or cover and refrigerate until used.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (Favorite Recipes for Family Meals Washington State University Extension)
desc_en: These yummy vegetarian burgers are made from lentils and are loaded with protein.

steps: Place lentils in a colander, rinse in cold water, and drain.
In a medium saucepan, bring water to a boil. Add lentils, reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 15 minutes.
Add onion and carrots. Cook 15 minutes more or until lentils are tender.
Remove from heat and cool slightly.
Stir in bread crumbs, egg, garlic powder, oregano, and salt.
Melt margarine or butter in large skillet. Drop lentil mixture by rounded 1/2 cupsful into hot margarine. Flatten mounds into patties and cook until firm and golden brown on both sides.
Top each patty with a thin slice of cheese.
Serve immediately.
Refrigerate leftovers within two hours.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (USDA Food and Nutrition Information Center)
desc_en: Fast and flavorful. Choose your favorite vegetables and try this quick and delicious dish on a busy weeknight. Serve with brown rice or quinoa.

steps: Preheat oven to 400 °F.
Cut four large rectangles of parchment paper or aluminum foil and fold in half to create a crease. Unfold.
Place each chicken breast in the middle of the foil or parchment paper and season with salt and pepper (if desired).
Top chicken with your choice of vegetables and seasonings.
Drizzle each packet with 1/2 teaspoon oil and 1 teaspoon lemon juice.
Fold the parchment paper or foil in half and then crimp around the edges tightly in 1/4-inch folds to create a half moon shape.
Using a spatula, transfer the packets to a baking sheet. Bake until the chicken is cooked to an internal temperature of 165 °F, about 20 minutes, depending the thickness of the chicken breast.
سخني الفرن على 200 درجة.
قطعي 4 ورقات كبار ديال الألومنيوم ولا ورق الفرن وطويهم على جوج ثم حليهم.
حطي كل صدر ديال الدجاج فوسط ورقة ورشي ملحة وإبزار.
حطي فوق الدجاج الخضرة اللي بغيتي: نص بصلة حمرا، خيزوة، فلفلة حمرا، عود كرافس ونص ݣرعة خضرا مقطعين، مع تومة مدقوقة وحبق وزعيترة ومعدنوس وسكنجبير.
صبي على كل بابيوط نص معلقة صغيرة زيت العود ومعلقة صغيرة عصير الحامض.
طوي الورق على جوج وسدي الجوانب مزيان بطيات صغار.
حطي البابيوطات فصينية ودخليهم 20 دقيقة حتى يطيب الدجاج على حسب الغلاضة ديالو.
tips: كل واحد فالعائلة يختار الخضرة ديالو فالبابيوط ديالو.
ما كاين والو للتنظيف، كلشي فالورق.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (USDA Food and Nutrition Information Center)
desc_en: Full of flavor, this easy fish recipe will quickly become a favorite. Make this different each time by adding in whatever vegetables you have at home. Serve over brown rice or quinoa.

steps: Preheat oven to 400 °F.
Cut four large rectangles of parchment paper or aluminum foil and fold in half to crease. Unfold.
Put each fish fillet on the foil or parchment paper and season with salt and pepper.
Top fish with your choice of vegetables and seasonings.
Drizzle each packet with 1/2 teaspoon oil and 1 teaspoon lemon juice.
Fold the parchment paper or foil in half and then crimp around the edges tightly in 1/4-inch folds to create a half moon shape.
Using a spatula, transfer the packets to a baking sheet. Bake until the fish is cooked to an internal temperature of 145 °F, about 10 to 12 minutes, depending the thickness of the fish.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (University of Connecticut Family Nutrition Program Senior Nutrition Awareness Project (SNAP) Newsletters)
desc_en: Try this soup on a cold evening as a start to your meal. Enjoy this soup with a side of salad, fruit, and whole grain bread.

steps: Peel and chop the onion.
Chop the celery into small pieces.
Put the celery and onion in a saucepan.
Add 1/2 cup chicken broth (save the other cup of chicken broth for later).
Cook these ingredients on low heat. Let the broth simmer for 2 to 3 minutes.
In a small bowl, mix the dry milk, flour, and pepper. Add them into the 1 cup of chicken broth that hasn't been cooked yet. Beat till smooth.
Add this mix to the celery, onion, and broth.
Cook over medium heat till the soup thickens.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (Iowa Department of Public Health Iowa Nutrition Network)
desc_en: Enjoy this tasty dip with carrots, radishes, celery, bell peppers, jicama, or whatever veggies you have on hand.

steps: Mix together ingredients.
Keep this simple dip in the fridge.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (Cooking Demo II Food and Health Communications, Inc.)
name_fr: Chaudrée de maïs en dix minutes
desc_en: Try this quick, easy, and creamy corn soup when you're short on time.

steps: Heat a large non-stick skillet over medium-high heat. Add the oil and sauté the onion and garlic until golden, about 2 minutes.
Meanwhile, place the flour, milk, mustard, and seasonings in a small bowl and mix well.
Add the milk mixture to the skillet followed by the corn; mix well until the mixture comes to a boil and thickens, for about 3 minutes. Stir frequently to keep the mixture from burning.
Divide into four bowls and top each with 1 tablespoon of shredded cheese.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (Simple Healthy Recipes Oklahoma Nutrition Information and Education ONIE Project)
desc_en: Lettuce wraps make great appetizers, or enjoy two for an entree. Pairs well with fresh or canned pineapple.

steps: Mix the water, cornstarch, and teriyaki sauce.
Add meat and water chestnuts.
Heat oil in a skillet or heavy saucepan and add meat and sauce mixture; stir until cooked through.
Serve in a lettuce leaf.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (University of Wisconsin Cooperative Extension Service Family Living Program)
desc_en: Quick and easy tacos, perfect for an easy weeknight meal. You can use homemade refried beans or canned refried beans for this recipe.

steps: Heat oil in skillet over medium heat. Add onion and cook until soft.
Add refried beans to skillet. Heat thoroughly.
Spread refried bean mixture in taco shells or on tortillas.
Sprinkle with shredded cheese, lettuce, chopped tomatoes, and taco sauce, as desired.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (Meeting Your MyPlate Goals on a Budget MyPlate National Strategic Partners Toolkit)
desc_en: This dish is packed with lean protein in the forms of black bean and lean ground beef. Chili powder, cumin, and fresh salsa add bold flavor to this Mexican-inspired recipe.

steps: Rinse lettuce, bell pepper, tomato, and jalapeño. Rinse and peel onion. Peel garlic.
Chop or shred lettuce into bite-sized pieces. Mince garlic. Cut the jalapeño and bell peppers in half. Remove seeds with the tip of a knife. Dice peppers.
Over a small bowl, grate tomato and onion using the coarse side of a box grater. Collect all pulp and juices.
Grate cheddar cheese.
In a colander, drain and rinse beans.
In a large skillet over medium-high heat, cook meat, bell pepper, and garlic until meat is lightly browned. Drain to remove fat.
Stir in frozen corn, beans, water, and spices. Bring mixture to a boil. Lower heat and cover. Simmer for 10 minutes, or until most liquid is gone.
While meat mixture is simmering, make a salsa. Add jalapeño and a pinch of salt to the grated tomato and onion. Stir and set aside.
Divide the meat mixture evenly among the 8 tortillas. Top each with grated cheese, salsa, and lettuce. Roll up and serve.
غسلي نص خس، فلفلة خضرا، ماطيشة وفلفلة حارة. قشري بصلة حمرا و2 حبات تومة.
قطعي الخس قطع صغار. دقي التومة. حيدي الزريعة من الفلفلة والفلفلة الحارة وقطعيهم صغار.

ممكن تستعملي كفتة الديك الرومي.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (Produce for Better Health Foundation)
desc_en: A deliciously sweet and savory dish featuring chicken, fresh pineapple, and red bell peppers.

ingredients.en: Boneless, skinless chicken breast, cut into 1" cubes
Red bell pepper, cut into chunks

steps: Cook rice according to package directions.
Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a large skillet. Add cubed chicken, stir fry 4 to 5 minutes until chicken is done. Remove from skillet.
Heat remaining oil. Add garlic and cook 1 minute.
Add bell pepper, onion, and broccoli; cook 5 minutes.
Add pineapple; cook an additional 3 to 4 minutes.
Return chicken to skillet and stir in juice from 1/2 lime, fish sauce, chili sauce, and cilantro. Cook 1 more minute.
Serve over brown rice with lime wedges.
طيبي 740 غ روز كامل.

زيدي معلقة زيت أخرى و2 حبات تومة مدقوقة، قلبي دقيقة.
زيدي فلفلة حمرا مقطعة قطع، بصلة مقطعة قطع و300 غ بروكلي، طيبيهم 5 دقايق.
زيدي 300 غ أناناس مقطع وطيبي 3 حتى 4 دقايق.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (Food Wise Learn at Home Print Materials Rutgers University Cooperative Extension)
desc_en: Try this sweet and tangy dressing on your favorite salad or as a dip for veggies.

steps: Mix ingredients together.
Chill and serve over vegetables or on a salad.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (The Bold and Beautiful Book of Bean Recipes Washington State WIC Program)
desc_en: This tasty salad pairs excellently with a tuna salad sandwich on whole grain bread and a piece of fruit. Make ahead of time and chill overnight in the refrigerator to let the flavor blend together.

steps: Mix beans, vegetables and garlic cloves in a large bowl.
Mix vinegar, oil, and sugar in a saucepan. Heat until sugar dissolves. Cool slightly.
Stir seasonings into vinegar mixture. Pour over vegetables. Toss lightly. Chill overnight.
Remove garlic before serving.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (Healthy Futures: Choosing Healthy Foods Virginia Cooperative Extension)
name_fr: Pain aux trois céréales et cacahuètes
name_latin: Khobz b tlata hboub o kawkaw
desc_en: Enjoy this scrumptious snack with your family. Use another nut butter if a member of your family suffers from a peanut allergy.

steps: Preheat oven to 325 °F.
Combine dry ingredients in a large bowl.
Using two knives, cut peanut butter into dry ingredients until it appears coarse and crumbly.
In a small bowl, beat together egg white and milk. Add to dry ingredients and mix well.
Spread mixture into a greased loaf pan. Bake at 325 °F for 1 hour and 10 minutes.
Cool for 10 minutes and remove from pan.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (Food Hero Oregon State University Cooperative Extension Service)
name_fr: Soupe des trois sœurs (maïs, haricots, courge)
name_latin: Chorbat dra o loubya o ger3a
desc_en: A true comfort recipe to warm you up year-round. Make it your own by using any vegetables or beans that you have on hand.

steps: Heat oil in a large pan on medium heat. Add carrot and onion and sauté until onions have begun to turn slightly brown, about 8 to 10 minutes.
Add garlic, squash, and corn and continue to stir for another 3 to 4 minutes.
Add beans, tomatoes, broth, cumin, and pepper.
Allow soup to come to a boil and then turn heat down to a simmer until all vegetables are tender to taste (15 to 30 minutes, depending on the vegetables used).

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (A Harvest of Recipes with USDA Foods USDA Food Distribution Program on Indian Reservations Adapted from a recipe submitted by Alicson Scott, Chickasaw Nation, Get Fresh! Nutrition Education Program)
name_latin: Merqat dra o loubya o ger3a
desc_en: This hearty stew is great for dinner and even better the next day. It uses different ingredients like sweet potatoes and quick-cooking oats.

steps: In a small skillet, brown ground beef and onions over medium to high heat for 8 to 10 minutes. Drain fat.
In a large pot, combine cooked ground beef, water, and red potatoes.
Bring the pot to a boil and cook for 15 minutes.
Add all the other ingredients to the pot and bring to a boil. Lower heat and simmer for about 25 minutes.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (Produce for Better Health Foundation)
desc_en: Let kids build mini pizzas. Top whole-grain pita with sauce and criss-cross of low-fat mozzarella cheese and vegetables for a quick, fun dinner.

steps: Place rack in middle of oven and pre-heat oven to 400 °F.
For Xs, cut carrot and bell pepper into small sticks about 2 inches long. For Os, cut summer squash into 12 slices. For grid, pull apart each cheese stick to make 4 strips.
Place pita rounds on baking sheet and spread pasta sauce on each.
Let kids build tic tac toe pizzas with cheese and vegetables.
Bake about 10 minutes or until cheese is bubbling.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion)
desc_en: Tofu cooked until golden brown, and broccoli sautéed in a soy and scallion sauce make up this one-skillet meal. Serve with a side of brown rice for a quick dish.

steps: Put the tofu on a cutting board and cut it in half and then cut each half into 4 equal pieces.
Put 2 layers of paper towel on a cutting board and put the tofu on top. Let drain at least 20 minutes (and up to 2 hours).
Place a skillet over medium heat and when hot, add 2 teaspoons oil. Add the tofu, one piece at a time, and cook until golden, about 3 minutes per side. Remove the tofu to a plate and set aside.

Reheat the skillet and when it is hot, add remaining 2 teaspoons oil. Add garlic and scallions and cook until just golden, about 2 minutes. Add the broccoli and water and raise the heat to high. Cook until the broccoli is tender, about 4 minutes.
Return the tofu to the pan and add the remaining ingredients. Stir well.
Serve with a side of brown rice.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (University of Connecticut Family Nutrition Program Senior Nutrition Awareness Project (SNAP) Newsletters)
desc_en: Searching for a good vegetarian lunch option? Enjoy this tofu and vegetable salad on whole grain bread, with a piece of fruit for a satisfying and tasty meal.

steps: Prepare tofu by draining the water from the package and placing tofu between two plates. Put a heavy object on top and let stand for 10 to 15 minutes. Drain the water that collects on the bottom plate every few minutes.
In a small bowl, mix the mayonnaise, mustard, and soy sauce.
In a medium bowl, combine the diced tofu, celery, onion, pepper, and parley; stir in the mayonnaise mixture and toss gently to coat.
Refrigerate covered until the flavors are blended -- at least one hour.
Use as a sandwich filling or on top of whole grain crackers.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (Montana State University Extension Service Nutrition Education Program)
name_latin: Chorbat tofu bel matecha o selq
desc_en: This vegetable and tofu soup is a delicious way to end your day. You can use fresh or frozen spinach and top with cilantro for a satisfying soup.

ingredients.en: Tofu, silken, firm or extra firm

steps: Heat a 3 quart saucepan over medium heat; add oil and chopped onion. Cook onion until softened, but not brown. Stir in garlic and cook just until fragrant.
Add chicken broth. Bring to a boil. Add tomatoes and tofu. Lower heat and simmer until tomatoes are soft but not mushy (this takes just a couple of minutes).
Stir in green onions (optional), spinach, ground pepper and cilantro. Cook just until spinach is wilted.
Remove from heat. Taste for seasoning. Serve hot.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (University of Nebraska at Lincoln Nebraska Nutrition Education Program)
desc_en: This refreshing salad is an excellent source of vitamin C and a great way to take advantage of the vegetables’ summer growing season.

steps: In a large bowl, combine the salad ingredients.
In a small bowl, mix the dressing ingredients together.
Pour the dressing over the salad. Mix well.
Refrigerate for at least 1 hour before serving.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (California Champions for Change: Breakfast Recipes California Department of Public Health Network for a Healthy California)
desc_en: Toasted garlic bread and mozzarella cheese combine with tomatoes and basil to give this easy omelet delicious, fresh flavor. Add a piece of fruit on the side to for a meal with food from each food group.

steps: Preheat oven to 300 °F.

Cut the bread into cubes; toss with oil and garlic in a small bowl. Spread the cubes in a single layer on a baking sheet and toast in the oven for 15 to 25 minutes, or until golden brown, tossing once or twice. Transfer to a plate to cool.
Spray a medium pan with nonstick cooking spray and heat over medium-high heat. Pour in egg substitute.
When the egg begins to set, spread evenly across the bottom of the pan and reduce the heat to low.

Once the top layer of egg is almost cooked, sprinkle the cheese and basil on top and scatter the tomatoes and bread over half of the omelet; fold the unfilled omelet half over the filling. Slide the omelet on a plate and serve.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (Farm Fresh Summertime Recipes Connecticut Food Policy Council)
name_en: Tomato Basil and Bean Pasta Salad
name_fr: Salade de pâtes tomate, basilic et haricots
name_latin: Chladat mqarouna bel matecha o hbeq o loubya
desc_en: Beans, tomatoes, and basil are mixed with pasta and a tasty vinaigrette to give you a easy and tasty meal. Bring this pasta salad to your next cookout or gathering. Add whatever vegetables you have on hand.

steps: Cook pasta according to package directions. Drain and cool.
In a small mixing bowl, whisk together vegetable oil, vinegar, Dijon-style mustard, and pepper to make vinaigrette.
In a large mixing bowl, combine pasta, beans, basil, and tomatoes. Pour vinaigrette over top and toss together. Cover and chill at least 1 hour.
If desired, add nuts and cheese just before serving, tossing again to combine.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (Healthy Eating Recipes University of Nebraska Cooperative Extension)
name_latin: Khobz mhammer bel matecha o hbeq
desc_en: This delicious appetizer is a great way to use ripe tomatoes and basil from your garden. Serve with toasted bread on the side for a quick and delicious appetizer for your family or at your next get-together.

steps: Preheat oven to 400 °F.
Combine tomatoes, garlic, onion, basil, and olive oil in a bowl. Season with salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste (optional). Set aside.
Arrange bread on a baking sheet in a single layer. Bake about 5 to 7 minutes until it begins to brown slightly.
Remove bread from oven and transfer to a serving platter.

Serve the tomato mixture in a bowl with a serving spoon and let everyone help themselves. Or place some on each slice of bread before serving. If adding the tomato mixture yourself, add it at the last minute or the bread may become soggy.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (USDA’s Collection of Nonfat Dry Milk Recipes USDA Food and Nutrition Service Food Distribution Service)
desc_en: This creamy soup can be prepared using pantry staples such as canned tomatoes and non-fat dry milk. Garlic and onion give this delicious soup an extra kick of flavor.

steps: In a medium saucepan, cook onion in oil over medium heat, stirring frequently until golden brown, about 4 minutes.
Add garlic and cook 1 minute longer. Add chopped tomatoes.
Cook uncovered over medium heat for 10 minutes.
Spoon 3/4 of mixture into food processor or blender container; puree until smooth. Return to saucepan.
Add red pepper, basil, and reconstituted milk to the soup.
Heat until hot, but do not boil.
Season to taste with salt and pepper (optional).
Serve immediately.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (Cooking For You or Two University of Wyoming Extension Cent$ible Nutrition Program)
desc_en: Pasta and tomato sauce are topped with cheese and cooked in the oven. Double this recipe for a family of 4. Add a tossed salad for a hearty meal.

steps: Cook pasta according to package directions; drain.
In a small saucepan, cook onion and garlic in oil until tender.
Stir in tomatoes, basil, oregano, sugar, and pepper.
Bring to a boil. Reduce heat. Simmer uncovered for 15 minutes. Add pasta to sauce.
Transfer to a greased 1-quart baking dish.
Top with cheeses.
Bake, uncovered at 375 °F for 10 to 15 minutes or until cheese is melted.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (Food and Health Communications, Inc.)
desc_en: Peas, lentils, and beans combined with spices and veggies provide this pasta soup with flavor and fiber. Enjoy this hearty soup on a chilly night.

steps: Rinse beans. Put into a 4 or 5 quart heavy pot with 8 cups of water. Bring to a boil, reduce heat to medium, cover, and simmer until the beans are tender (1 1/4 to 1 1/2 hours).
Add 4 cups water, seasonings, tortellini, carrots and celery to beans. Return to boil. Reduce heat to low, cover and simmer 1/2 hour, until tortellini and vegetables are tender.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (Healthy Latino Recipes Made with Love California Department of Health Services California Latino 5-A-Day Campaign)
desc_en: These mini pizzas combine the flavors of tacos with the fun and variety of pizza. A favorite for kids and adults alike.

ingredients.en: Vegetables, such as broccoli, mushrooms, spinach, and red bell pepper

steps: Brush one side of each of two tortillas with water. Press the wet sides of the tortillas together to form a thick crust for the pizza.
Brush the outside of the tortillas with a small amount of oil or margarine. Evenly brown both sides in a heated frying pan. Repeat with the rest of the tortillas. Set aside.
Heat refried beans, onion, and half of the chili peppers together in a medium saucepan, stirring occasionally. Remove from heat.

Spread about 1/3 cup of the bean mixture on each tortilla pizza. Sprinkle with 1 tablespoon taco sauce, then top with 1/2 cup of the chopped vegetables, 1 teaspoon chili peppers, and 1 tablespoon cheese for each pizza.
Return to frying pan and heat until cheese melts. Top with cilantro, if desired. Serve immediately.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (Cooking Up Fun - A Pyramid of Snacks Cornell Cooperative Extension Cornell University Division of Nutritional Sciences)
name_fr: Chips de tortilla et dip de haricots
desc_en: Prepare this layered dip with beans, salsa, sour cream, and cheese for your next party. Make your own tortilla chips to serve on the side. Fill up on fiber while having fun.

steps: Preheat oven to 400 °F.
Place tortillas in a stack on cutting board. With a sharp knife, cut stack into eight pieces, forming triangles or wedges.
Lay tortillas pieces out in single layer on baking sheet. Set aside while making dip.
Open canned beans. Pour beans in colander; rinse and drain. Place beans in a small mixing bowl and mash with a potato masher. Spread beans over bottom of baking dish.
Measure salsa and spread over beans.
Measure sour cream and spread over beans.
Grate and measure cheese; sprinkle over bean mixture.
Place lettuce wedge on cutting board. Slice into thin strips; set aside.

Place both the baking sheet with tortilla pieces and the dip in preheated oven. Bake about 8 minutes or until tortilla pieces are crisp and dip is bubbly. Sprinkle lettuce over dip and serve with tortilla chips.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (The Texas A&M University System Texas A&M AgriLife Extension Service Expanded Food and Nutrition Education Program)
desc_en: Crisp tortillas, refried beans, and layers of fresh veggies make this a tasty and healthy vegetarian option.

steps: Turn on oven to 350 °F.
Place tortillas on a cookie sheet and put in oven for 10 minutes or until crispy.
Wash lettuce and tomatoes. Shred lettuce and dice tomatoes
Spread two large tablespoons of refried beans on each tortilla.
Top with lettuce, tomatoes, and cheese. Add green onions if desired.
Serve immediately and refrigerate leftovers.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (University of Nebraska Nebraska Nutrition Education Program)
desc_en: A toasty tortilla with beans and melted cheese, topped with cool fresh veggies!

steps: Preheat oven to 350 °F.
On a baking sheet, arrange tortillas in a single layer. Spray both sides with non-stick cooking spray and bake for 4 minutes or until crisp.
If desired mix chili powder into refried beans.
Spoon 1/3 cup of refried beans on each tostada. Sprinkle with cheese.
Bake for 10 minutes or until cheese is melted.
Top each one with lettuce and tomato.
Serve with salsa and sour cream (optional).

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (University of Wisconsin Cooperative Extension Service)
desc_en: You can adjust this recipe to accommodate food allergies. Try with sunflower seed butter or almond butter if you are working with a peanut allergy.

steps: Combine dry ingredients in bowl.
Combine honey and sugar in pan and bring to a boil.
Add peanut butter and vanilla, stir until peanut butter melts.
Pour mixture over cereal and mix well.
Press into a 13x9 inch pan and cool.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (Food Hero Oregon State University Cooperative Extension Service)
desc_en: Throw together this quick treat full of dried fruit, nuts, and delicious grains. Enjoy it as a snack on your next walk through the park or hike.

steps: Choose the ingredients you want to use.
Measure the suggested amounts of chosen ingredients and add to mixing bowl.
Mix ingredients using stirring spoon and divide evenly into 4 storage bags.
Enjoy your Trail Treat!

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (University of Wyoming Extension Cent$ible Nutrition Program)
desc_en: Enjoy this tasty fruit dish in the morning or as a snack anytime of the day.

steps: Place orange juice in bowl.
Wash apple and dry. Remove the seeds and dice. Coat apple surfaces with orange juice to prevent browning.
Peel orange and break into sections. Cut sections into small pieces.
Peel and slice banana into 1/4 inch circles.
Combine all fruit and orange juice lightly in a bowl and mix together. Chill or serve immediately.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (Produce for Better Health)
name_latin: Choufan dyal lil bel fwakeh istiwa2iya
desc_en: Breakfast is a snap with a quick step the night before. Mix oats with yogurt and refrigerate overnight. Add bananas and pineapple chunks in the morning.

steps: Mix oats, milk, yogurt and allspice in two bowls or glass jars.
Cover and refrigerate overnight.
Just before serving, add pineapple, banana, and almonds.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion)
desc_en: Enjoy a tropical treat with these frozen yogurt pops! They are fun to make and have 1/4 cup of fruit per serving!

steps: Place all ingredients into blender.
Blend on high until smooth.
Pour into 4 small paper cups (or 8 ice cubes) and place in popsicle sticks (or cut paper straws).
Freeze.
Enjoy as a frozen treat!

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (Produce for Better Health Foundation)
name_fr: Sandwich salade de thon aux pommes
desc_en: Liven up your lunch-time sandwich with a refreshing mix of tuna, apples, raisins, and walnuts.

steps: Cut apple in quarters; remove core and chop.
In a medium-sized bowl, mix all salad ingredients, except tuna.
Gently fold in tuna.
Make sandwiches using lettuce and whole-grain bread (toasted, if desired), and fill with tuna apple salad.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (Discover the Secret to Healthy Living California Department of Health Services California Children’s 5-A-Day Power Play Campaign)
desc_en: Pita bread stuffed with salad greens, tuna, veggies, and fruit makes an easy and flavorful lunch or dinner.

steps: In a small bowl, stir together tuna, onion, apple, celery, raisins, and 2 tablespoons of dressing.
In another bowl, toss together salad greens with remaining dressing.
Carefully open pita breads and fill with equal amounts of greens and tuna salad.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (Texas Cooperative Extension Expanded Nutrition Program The Texas A&M University System)
desc_en: Delicious and easy, this tuna melt makes a yummy lunch or dinner. Each sandwich bakes in it's own foil package, so there's an added bonus of easy cleanup.

steps: Preheat oven to 350 °F.
Drain tuna and break the meat apart with a fork.
Wash and chop the celery and shred the cheese.
Mix tuna, celery, cheese, light mayonnaise, dried onion, salt, and pepper into a medium mixing bowl with a wooden spoon.
Divide tuna mixture into six portions, place one portion on six slices of whole wheat bread. Then place a single slice of bread on top of each. (you will make a total of 6 sandwiches).
Wrap each sandwich on a square of aluminum foil, folding edges securely.
Bake about 20 minutes or until hot in the middle. Cool slightly before serving.
Remove from oven. Pierce foil to release steam before serving.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (Simple Healthy Recipes Oklahoma Nutrition Information and Education ONIE Project)
desc_en: This hearty pasta dish uses pantry staples such as canned tuna and cream soup along with a few fresh veggies to make a dish full of protein and flavor.

ingredients.en: Cream of mushroom soup, reduced sodium

steps: Cook pasta according to package directions and drain.
In a large skillet or pot, cook onion and pepper in oil.
Add cream soup, diced tomatoes and tuna to onion and pepper.
Mix with pasta. Put in baking dish.
Cook at 350 °F for 25 minutes until bubbly.
Top with cheese and parsley if desired and return to oven for 5 minutes to melt.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (Eating Smart, Being Active Colorado State University and University of California at Davis)
desc_en: Loaded with protein-packed tuna, nutritious veggies and fresh cooked pasta, this dish makes a delicious meal.

steps: Cook spaghetti according to package; drain.
Heat oil in a large skillet or pan over medium heat. Add onion and broccoli (or zucchini). Cook until softened.
Stir in tomato-based pasta sauce. Bring to a boil. Turn heat to low and simmer for 3 minutes.
Add drained tuna into the sauce mixture. Stir just enough to heat the tuna.
Add salt and pepper to taste (optional). Add cooked spaghetti to the sauce. Stir the pasta and sauce mixture until mixed together uniformly.
Optional: Add 2 tablespoons Parmesan cheese to cooked mixture of pasta and sauce.
Serve hot.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (Adapted from Tuna Salad, Eating Smart, Being Active Colorado State University and University of California at Davis)
desc_en: Grapes make this tuna salad both savory and sweet. Serve this salad over lettuce leaves for a quick and easy lunch.

steps: In a medium-sized bowl, combine drained tuna, celery, mayonnaise and yogurt and stir.
Add grapes to mixture and stir gently.
Cover and chill until ready to serve.
Serve over lettuce leaves.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (Cooking Demo II Food and Health Communications, Inc.)
desc_en: Tuna salad served on a bed of lettuce and veggies with a whole grain crackers on the side makes this an easy and delicious lunch. Have a piece of fruit as a tasty side dish or dessert.

steps: Toss lettuce, vegetables, oil, vinegar and herbs in a large salad bowl.
Mix ingredients for tuna salad in another medium sized mixing bowl.
Assemble salad by placing greens on a large plate. Top with a scoop of tuna salad.
Serve crackers on the side.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (Eating Smart, Being Active Colorado State University and University of California at Davis)
desc_en: Grapes make this tuna salad both savory and sweet. Serve this salad over lettuce leaves for a quick and easy lunch.

steps: In a medium-sized bowl, combine drained tuna, celery, mayonnaise and yogurt and stir.
Add grapes to mixture and stir gently.
Cover and chill until ready to serve.
Serve over lettuce leaves.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (Cans Get You Cooking)
name_fr: Mini-burgers de thon aux piments verts
name_latin: Burger sghir bel ton o felfla khadra
desc_en: For a touch of spice and everything nice, add some canned green chilies to tuna sliders. You won't believe how much flavor this canned staple packs in! With a well-stocked pantry full of canned ingredients, like tuna and green chilies, it’s easy to create delicious, homemade meals you can feel good about serving your family and friends.

steps: In large bowl, combine tuna, green chilies, celery, red onion, mayonnaise, and chopped cilantro; toss to mix well.
Add lettuce leaves to the bottom half of each roll.
Top with some tuna mixture.
Add top half of roll and enjoy!

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (Farm Fresh Summertime Recipes Connecticut Food Policy Council)
desc_en: Herbs really give this salad a real zest. Marinate overnight in the refrigerator to allow flavors to blend. If you don't have the vegetables listed, substitute whatever veggies you have on hand.

steps: Wash and trim vegetables. Chop into bite-sized pieces. Place in large bowl.
Combine vinegar, dill (or other herbs), garlic, and oil. Pour over vegetables.
Drain and rinse beans. Break up tuna into smaller chunks.
Combine vegetables, beans, and tuna; toss gently.
Marinate salad overnight to combine flavors.
Chill and serve as a light summer lunch or as a picnic side dish.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (Created by the Grain Foods Foundation, a member of the MyPlate National Strategic Partnership Program)
desc_en: It's time to raise the bar on the good ol’ tuna sandwich. Boost flavor with lemon juice and Dijon. Seasonal veggies in the mix do double-duty – taste and color!

ingredients.en: Romaine lettuce leaves, torn in half

steps: In a small bowl, mix together tuna, mayonnaise, Dijon mustard, and lemon juice.
Stir in carrots, red bell peppers, and celery. Place 6 torn leaves of romaine lettuce on half of the slices of whole wheat bread.
Spoon tuna mixture on top of the lettuce slices.
Place another torn lettuce slice on each tuna sandwich and cover with another slice of bread.
Wrap sandwiches in colorful plastic wrap or wax paper and keep chilled.
Your sandwiches are now picnic ready!

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (MyPlate National Strategic Partners The Grain Chain)
desc_en: These sandwiches, flavored with herbs and spices, are sure to hit the spot. With whole grains, lean protein, and dairy, this well-rounded, MyPlate meal will keep you satisfied all afternoon.

steps: Mix the yogurt, dill, onion, pepper, and chopped cucumbers.
Divide the yogurt/ cucumber mixture on all 8 slices of bread.
Top the whole wheat bread with turkey and cucumber slices.
Cover with the white bread slices.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (Simple Healthy Recipes Oklahoma Nutrition Information and Education ONIE Project)
desc_en: Lemon juice give these zesty burgers a real treat for your next cookout. Serve with tomatoes, lettuce, onion, and a whole wheat bun to boost your veggie and whole grains for the day.

steps: Combine onions, turkey, lemon juice, Worcestershire sauce, and parsley. Mix well.
Shape mixture into four patties.
Fry in a pan on medium heat or grill until internal temperature reaches 165 °F.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (Pictorial Recipes Oregon State University Cooperative Extension Service Oregon Family Nutrition Program Recipe submitted by Lynn Myers Steele, 2000)
desc_en: This gravy uses chicken or turkey broth to create an easy and fast gravy. Perfect for a big holiday meal.

ingredients.fr: Bouillon de poulet ou de dinde

steps: Melt margarine in skillet over low heat. Mix in flour and salt. Stir and heat until bubbly.
Add broth slowly, stirring constantly. Cook over low heat for 5 to 10 minutes.
Add the cooked giblets. Heat a few minutes to blend flavors.
Store leftovers in refrigerator within 2 hours.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (Delicious Heart-Healthy Latino Recipes/ Platillos Latinos Sabrosos y Saludables US Department of Health and Human Services National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute)
desc_en: Toss some sweet potatoes in the oven when you're baking this meatloaf, and pair this dinner with a tossed salad for a tasty and delicious meal!

steps: Preheat oven to 350 °F.
Combine all ingredients and mix well.
Bake in 9x5 loaf pan for 25 minutes or until it reaches an internal temperature of 165 °F. Check the temperature with a meat thermometer.
Cut into five slices and serve.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (Quick and Healthy Meals: Tips and Tools for Planning Meals for Your Family Ohio State University Cooperative Extension Cuyahoga County)
desc_en: Enjoy these tasty patties with fresh tomato slices and your favorite condiments on a whole grain bun.

steps: Mix ground turkey, bread crumbs, egg, onions, and mustard in a large bowl. Shape into 4 patties, about 1/2 inch thick.
Spray a large skillet with cooking spray. Add patties and cook, turning once to brown other side. Cook until golden brown outside and white inside, about 10 minutes. Remove.
Add chicken broth to skillet and boil over high heat until slightly thickened, about 1 to 2 minutes. Pour sauce over patties.
فطبسيل كبير خلطي 570 غ كفتة الديك الرومي، 110 غ شابلور، بيضة، 40 غ بصلة خضرا مقطعة و3 معالق صغار موطارد. صاوبي 4 كفتات غلاضهم 1 سم.
دهني مقلة كبيرة بشوية زيت. حطي الكفتات وطيبيهم 10 دقايق، وقلبيهم مرة، حتى يحمرو من برا ويطيبو من الداخل. خرجيهم.
زيدي 70 مل مرقة الدجاج للمقلة وخليها تغلي على نار قوية دقيقة ولا جوج حتى تخثر شوية. صبيها فوق الكفتات.
tips: ما تعصريش الكفتة بزاف ملي تصاوبيها باش تبقى طرية.
ممكن تستعملي كفتة الدجاج ولا البݣري.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (Ohio State University Cooperative Extension)
desc_en: Colorful tomatoes and spinach make these appetizers festive enough for your next party or potluck.

steps: Place tortillas on microwaveable plate or paper towel; microwave uncovered on HIGH 10 to 15 seconds to soften.
Spread about 2 tablespoons cream cheese over each tortilla. Top with a slice of turkey, chopped tomatoes, and spinach.
Roll up lightly; then wrap in plastic wrap. Refrigerate 2 to 3 hours to blend flavors.
Cut each roll into eight 1-inch slices. Arrange with cut side down on serving plate.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (University of Maine Cooperative Extension)
name_fr: Salade de pommes de terre à la dinde
desc_en: Green pepper, onions, and celery give this salad a delicious crunch. Serve chilled on a bed of lettuce or whole grain bread.

steps: Mix turkey, celery, potato, onion, and green pepper.
Mix mayonnaise, mustard and salt. Stir lightly into turkey mixture.
Chill.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (Cook it QUICK! University of Nebraska Cooperative Extension)
name_fr: Salade de dinde, vinaigrette à l'orange
name_latin: Chladat dik roumi b salsat letchin
desc_en: Fresh orange juice and Dijon mustard give this vinaigrette a bright and zesty flavor to top this turkey and orange salad.

steps: In a jar with tight-fitting lid, combine all vinaigrette ingredients; shake well. If you don't have a container with a tight-fitting lid, place ingredients in a small mixing bowl and mix together with a whisk.
In large bowl, combine all salad ingredients; toss gently.
Serve with vinaigrette.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (Montana State University Extension Service)
desc_en: This hearty stew of turkey, potatoes, and vegetables will warm up a cold winter night. You can replace the cooked turkey with cooked chicken.

steps: Heat oil in medium saucepan. Add onion, garlic, carrots, and celery and stir for 2 minutes.
Add potatoes, tomatoes, and water to pan. Bring to a boil, then lower heat and simmer 30 minutes or until vegetables are tender. Add turkey and cook another five minutes or until heated.
Season to taste before serving.

source_text: USDA MyPlate Kitchen (A Healthier You: Based on the Dietary Guidelines for Americans US Department of Health and Human Services Office of Disease Prevention and Health Promotion)
desc_en: Turkey and ground beef stuffed cabbage leaves are cooked and topped with a sweet and savory sauce of veggies, lemon juice, and brown sugar.

steps: Rinse and core cabbage. Carefully remove 10 outer leaves, place in saucepan, and cover with boiling water. Simmer 5 minutes. Remove and drain cooked cabbage leaves on paper towels.
Shred 1/2 cup of raw cabbage and set aside.
